Variance Inflation Factor Table

Source: R/VIF.table.R
VIF.table.Rd

Computes variance inflation factors (VIFs) for the terms of a regression to diagnose multicollinearity, and returns them as a LaTeX table (for PDF reports) or plain text (for the console), like the other snazzieR summary tables. car is not required.

Usage

VIF.table(
  model,
  title = "Variance Inflation Factors",
  latex = TRUE,
  cols = "all",
  moderate = 5,
  severe = 10,
  digits = 4
)

Arguments

model

A fitted lm or glm object with at least two terms.

title

Table title (its LaTeX caption). Defaults to "Variance Inflation Factors".

latex

Logical; if TRUE (default) returns a LaTeX table. If FALSE, prints a plain-text table and returns the underlying data frame invisibly.

cols

Columns to show: "all" (default) or any combination of "VIF", "1/VIF", "GVIF" and "adj. GVIF". Term and Flag are always included.

moderate, severe

VIF cutoffs for flagging moderate and severe multicollinearity. Default 5 and 10.

digits

Number of significant digits shown. Defaults to 4.

Value

If latex = TRUE, a LaTeX table of class "snazzieR_table" (see snazzieR_table for interactive previews). If latex = FALSE, the table is printed and a data frame of the shown columns, one row per term, is returned invisibly.

Details

VIFs are computed from the correlation matrix of the estimated coefficients, exactly as car::vif() does, so they are valid for weighted lm fits and for glm fits. For a numeric predictor, \(\mathrm{VIF}_j = 1/(1 - R^2_j)\), where \(R^2_j\) is from regressing that predictor on all the others.

The available columns are:

VIF

The variance inflation factor. Terms with more than one coefficient (factors, poly(), splines) have no ordinary VIF, so their VIF is reported as \((\textrm{adj. GVIF})^2\), which is on the same scale and equals the ordinary VIF for one-df terms.

1/VIF

The tolerance, \(1 - R^2_j\).

GVIF

The generalized VIF of Fox and Monette (1992); equal to the VIF for one-df terms.

adj. GVIF

\(\mathrm{GVIF}^{1/(2\,\mathrm{Df})}\), comparable across terms with different degrees of freedom. Each cell also shows the term's degrees of freedom, e.g. 1.547 (df = 2).

The Term and Flag columns are always shown. Terms are flagged moderate when the VIF exceeds moderate (default 5) and severe when it exceeds severe (default 10). Rows are sorted from the highest VIF to the lowest. Aliased (perfectly collinear) coefficients are dropped and listed in the notes under the table.

References

Fox, J. and Monette, G. (1992). Generalized collinearity diagnostics. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 87, 178–183.

See also

unusual.points.table, model.summary.table

Examples

model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + disp + qsec, data = mtcars)
VIF.table(model, latex = FALSE)
#> == Variance Inflation Factors ==
#> 
#> 
#> Term   VIF     1/VIF    GVIF    adj. GVIF        Flag     
#> -----  ------  -------  ------  ---------------  ---------
#> disp   7.985   0.1252   7.985   2.826 (df = 1)   moderate 
#> wt     6.917   0.1446   6.917   2.63 (df = 1)    moderate 
#> hp     5.167   0.1935   5.167   2.273 (df = 1)   moderate 
#> qsec   3.133   0.3192   3.133   1.77 (df = 1)             
#> 
#> Moderate: VIF > 5.  Severe: VIF > 10.  Mean VIF = 5.8.
#> adj. GVIF = GVIF^(1/(2 Df)).

# Factors get generalized VIFs
VIF.table(lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + factor(cyl), data = mtcars), latex = FALSE)
#> == Variance Inflation Factors ==
#> 
#> 
#> Term          VIF     1/VIF    GVIF    adj. GVIF        Flag 
#> ------------  ------  -------  ------  ---------------  -----
#> hp            3.496   0.286    3.496   1.87 (df = 1)         
#> wt            2.581   0.3875   2.581   1.607 (df = 1)        
#> factor(cyl)   2.26    0.4426   5.106   1.503 (df = 2)        
#> 
#> Moderate: VIF > 5.  Severe: VIF > 10.  Mean VIF = 2.78.
#> adj. GVIF = GVIF^(1/(2 Df)).  For multi-df terms, VIF = (adj. GVIF)^2.

# Only some columns
VIF.table(model, latex = FALSE, cols = c("VIF", "1/VIF"))
#> == Variance Inflation Factors ==
#> 
#> 
#> Term   VIF     1/VIF    Flag     
#> -----  ------  -------  ---------
#> disp   7.985   0.1252   moderate 
#> wt     6.917   0.1446   moderate 
#> hp     5.167   0.1935   moderate 
#> qsec   3.133   0.3192            
#> 
#> Moderate: VIF > 5.  Severe: VIF > 10.  Mean VIF = 5.8.

# LaTeX table for a PDF report
tbl <- VIF.table(model, title = "Collinearity Check")
